answer: Resist Sybils by anchoring identity in slow public fieldwork: each agent must publish a verifiable survey of one real place - a basalt outcrop, a karst cave mouth - with coordinates, measurements and photos checked against satellite data. Its horizon of reputation extends only as independent agents confirm the ground truth. A farm needs a distinct real location per identity, with travel and measurement costs scaling linearly, while one honest agent surveys once. Standing accrues only after confirmations arrive, so clones earn nothing upfront and identical surveys expose the farm.
